original_question: Do there exist fast convergent sequences (x_n) such that the adjoint Cantorval E(x_n) is achievable?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 36 ("Center of distances"): the open problem asking whether an adjoint Cantorval can be an achievable set for some fast convergent sequence.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the precise open-problem theme in the paper: an existence question about fast convergent sequences and whether the associated adjoint Cantorval can be achievable. It also stays narrow and does not drift into broader questions about arbitrary Cantorvals or general achievement sets.
missing_details: The ambient setting is the real line, with sequences in l_1 of real numbers; in the central-Cantor-set correspondence used here, the sequence is a positive absolutely summable real sequence.
"Fast convergent" should be made explicit: for the associated positive sequence x=(x_n), one has x_n>r_n for every n, where r_n:=sum_{k>n} x_k.
The achievement-set operator must be defined: E(x):={sum_{n=1}^infty epsilon_n x_n : (epsilon_n) in {0,1}^N}.
In the paper's normalization, the associated central Cantor set has fundamental interval [0,1], equivalently sum_{n=1}^infty x_n=1.
The adjoint Cantorval is not E(x) itself; it is built from the central Cantor set C=E(x).
One must define U_n as the union of all open intervals removed at the n-th step of the central Cantor-set construction of C.
The adjoint Cantorval should be specified as the set obtained by deleting only the even-step gaps, equivalently keeping C together with all odd-step removed intervals.
"Achievable" should be spelled out as: there exists some absolutely summable real sequence y such that the adjoint Cantorval equals E(y).
refined_question: Does there exist a positive fast convergent sequence x=(x_n) in l_1 with sum_{n=1}^infty x_n=1 and x_n>r_n:=sum_{k>n}x_k for every n, such that, if C=E(x)={sum_{n=1}^infty epsilon_n x_n : (epsilon_n) in {0,1}^N} is the associated central Cantor set in [0,1] and U_n denotes the union of all open intervals removed at stage n in the central construction of C, then its adjoint Cantorval A(C):=[0,1]\setminus \bigcup_{n\ge 1}U_{2n}=C\cup\bigcup_{n\ge 1}U_{2n-1} is achievable, i.e. A(C)=E(y) for some absolutely summable real sequence y?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, does there exist a central Cantor set C with fundamental interval [0,1] whose adjoint Cantorval is an achievement set?
justification: The phrase "adjoint Cantorval" appears in the paper only in Section 7, where Problem 36 states almost exactly the question your draft is aiming at. The nearby context first defines the adjoint Cantorval for a central Cantor set, and earlier context in Section 3 explains that central Cantor sets with fundamental interval [0,1] are exactly the achievement sets of positive fast convergent series of total sum 1. That is why a fully stand-alone version must quantify over a positive fast convergent sequence x, define E(x), define the stage-wise removed intervals U_n and the adjoint Cantorval built from them, and then spell out that "achievable" means equal to E(y) for some absolutely summable sequence y. The alternate formulation is justified by the explicit bijection in Section 3 between such sequences and central Cantor sets.
